long_description:
Up! Go! More! is a bright, uncluttered first-words book for babies and toddlers, built for laps and back-and-forth. Each of its 22 pages shows one everyday word a little one really uses, from hi and peekaboo to eat, help, more, all done and night-night. The word is set in huge rounded letters above one big, friendly picture.

Every page also gives you two small things to do together. A Say it, Sign it or Act it cue offers one sound, simple hand sign or move to copy, like tapping fingertips for more or hiding your eyes for peekaboo. A short grown-up tip turns reading into a back-and-forth chat: pause and wait, add one word, offer a choice, copy each other, or follow your child's lead. A look, a point, a sign or a tap on a talking device all count as a turn. There is no script and nothing to get right. Pick any tip and skip any tip.

The front pages explain how to read together in four plain steps. The back pages show where the words live in your day, from mealtime to bedtime, and include a keepsake word list, pages to add your family's own words, and a free printable bonus for grown-ups. The paperback has paper pages: read it together, and keep it away from mouths.

Up! Go! More! is Book 1 of the Talk-Along Firsts series. Next come sounds and animals, then routines and feelings.

compliance_notes: No health or medical claims: this is a parent-education picture book, not a treatment or professional service of any kind, and it claims no outcome for any child. It is not presented as written by a speech-language professional, and no diagnosis or condition is named or targeted in its text, keywords or ads (BRAND.md hard rule 1 and the diagnosis-search rule). Talk strategies are described in plain words, with no trademarked program names. No real brands, logos, schools or products; the tablet on the night-night page is a generic, neutral object. No research citations are used. Hand signs are described as simple signs, not as a sign-language course. The inside pages say that every child talks on their own timeline and point parents to their child's doctor with questions. Safety: no small objects are suggested (blocks, a ball, a cup and a duck toy only; no food choking hazards) and adult reading together is assumed. The paperback has paper pages, so the copyright page says 'Paper pages: read together and keep away from mouths' and the listing says the same (customer-voice rule 20); the 'Add your own words' page is a grown-up keepsake page, not a child mark-making page. Talk tips include 'Talk, sing and read in the language you know best. Every language counts.' (rule 15). Both editions carry 'Version 1.0 · September 2026' on the copyright page (rule 3); bump it and tell past buyers on any file change. Grown-up tip labels and cue chips on sun-yellow pages use ink text for contrast. faq.q: Are the hand signs from a sign language?
faq.a: They are simple everyday signs many families use, described in plain words. The book is not a sign-language course.

faq.q: My child signs, points or uses a talking device. Is this book a good fit?
faq.a: Yes. The book says it plainly: a look, a point, a sign, a sound or a tap on a talking device is your child's turn.

faq.q: We speak another language at home. Can we use it?
faq.a: Yes. Talk, sing and read in the language you know best; every language counts. Say each word in your home language, and use the 'Add your own words' page for your family's words. There is no Spanish or bilingual edition yet.

faq.q: Can I read it aloud at storytime or in class?
faq.a: Yes, reading the printed book aloud to a group in person is welcome. For a recorded or online read-aloud, ask first through the contact form at playbeforepixels.com.

faq.q: Can we order copies for a class, child-care center, library or family night?
faq.a: Yes. Use the quote form at playbeforepixels.com. Copies are printed on demand and shipped straight to you by the printer, with an emailed invoice.
Printing mistakes or damage are replaced by the store you bought from. See playbeforepixels.com for the full refund policy.
